chunks: And Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Shuʿayb ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
When the deceased dies, then the sword, the saddle, and the clothes — the clothes of his person — belong to his eldest son.

key_terms.السَّيْفَ: the sword as a specified inherited item
key_terms.ثِيَابَ جِلْدِهِ: the clothing worn on his body, meaning his personal garments

ai.seo_question: What personal belongings of a deceased man go to his eldest son in Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding inheritance: certain personal effects of the deceased are assigned to his eldest son. It specifically mentions the sword, the saddle, and the clothing worn on his body as items designated for him.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5747 - Hammad ibn Isa narrated from Shuayb ibn Yaʿqub from Abu Basir from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) who said:
"When a man dies, his eldest son inherits the sword, the saddle, and his personal clothing."
